name: Pioneer Venus Small Probes
intro: Three identical small probes, named North, Day and Night, plunged into different parts of Venus on 9 December 1978. None was built to land, but all three reached the ground, and the Day Probe kept talking from the surface for more than an hour. Nobody can visit them on the scorching ground, so this model floats above Venus’s clouds as a memorial.
whyLeft: They were one-way probes, dropped without parachutes. On Venus’s 460 °C surface, their batteries and electronics soon gave out.
repurpose: They cannot be repaired. What they teach is how tough a Venus lander must be: the Day Probe’s 67 minutes on the ground showed it can be done.

hotspots.title: The Day Probe
hotspots.text: The Day Probe hit the ground and kept sending signals for 67 minutes, even though it was never designed to survive landing. Then the heat finished it.

source.label: NASA NSSDCA: Pioneer Venus Day Probe

hotspots.title: No parachutes
hotspots.text: The small probes had no parachutes. Venus’s air is so thick that it slowed them down on its own, and they kept their heat shields on all the way to the ground.

source.label: NASA NSSDCA: Pioneer Venus Day Probe

hotspots.title: Triplets far apart
hotspots.text: North, Day and Night were aimed thousands of kilometers apart. Measuring three places at once showed how the temperature and winds change across Venus.

hotspots.title: The mother ship
hotspots.text: All four probes rode to Venus on a mother ship called the bus. After letting them go, the bus dove in too and measured the thin upper air until it burned up.

photo.alt: Painting of a ring-shaped spacecraft in space, near the edge of Venus.
photo.caption: A NASA painting of the bus that carried all four probes, after it let them go.
